title: LLM evaluation and alignment
summary: Scientific evaluation from task definitions and annotation to uncertainty, deployment decisions and preference optimization. Includes exact CPU mechanisms and small real PyTorch training runs with explicit inference boundaries.

lessons.title: Evaluation contracts, populations and estimands
lessons.outcome: Define which population, unit, loss and decision an evaluation estimates, and demonstrate why a different denominator can reverse its conclusion.
lessons.lab: Compute B minus A and then A minus B for one success gained by B.
lessons.verification: The reversed comparison gives +1 and -1, the reweighted improvement is 0.5, a duplicated identifier and an empty population are rejected, and observed accuracy 1 is reported beside label coverage 0.5.

lessons.title: Evaluation data, grouping and contamination
lessons.outcome: Build a reproducible family/time split and detect identifier, near-duplicate and availability-time leakage before scoring.
lessons.lab: Put two paraphrases from one family into train and test.
lessons.verification: Paraphrases split across partitions fail family validation, a row at the cutoff is eligible under the inclusive policy while a delayed label is excluded, normalization changes the fingerprint, and historical evaluation uses the earlier corpus version.

lessons.title: Annotation rubrics and construct validity
lessons.outcome: Turn an intended capability into auditable labels, distinguish disagreement from missing evidence, and preserve adjudication history.
lessons.lab: Score one level 2 criterion and one inapplicable criterion.
lessons.verification: A response with one applicable dimension scores 1.0, a critical failure blocks admission, malformed labels and mixed rubric versions are rejected, both disagreeing labels stay in the ledger, and the proxy counterexample formats correctly while failing evidence support.

lessons.title: Agreement, prevalence and adjudication uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Calculate agreement with the correct marginals, explain prevalence effects, and distinguish reliable labels from valid labels.
lessons.lab: Rebuild the table in case A by counting label pairs.
lessons.verification: The confusion table is [[2, 0], [1, 1]]; perfect agreement gives kappa 1 and complete disagreement -1; the single-category case is rejected as undefined; and the sample still has two families when the dependence unit changes.

lessons.title: Stratified sampling and population weighting
lessons.outcome: Estimate a declared target mixture from an intentionally balanced evaluation and diagnose overlap and weight concentration.
lessons.lab: Use 25% routine and 75% rare in case A.
lessons.verification: The reweighted target accuracy is 0.6; missing support and zero inclusion probability are rejected; the known-size and sampled-weight denominators give 0.2 and 1/3; concentrated weights drive the effective sample size below 1.03; both systems use identical IDs and weights.

lessons.title: Paired comparisons and clustered uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Compute paired and family-level uncertainty while distinguishing a randomization null, a bootstrap approximation and a deployment claim.
lessons.lab: Use paired differences 0,0.
lessons.verification: Vanishing differences give an exact tail of 1, four favorable pairs give 2/16 = 0.125, relabeling leaves the two-sided p-value unchanged, the two quantile conventions give about +/-0.925 and +/-1, and three families have 27 ordered bootstrap draws.

lessons.title: Multiplicity and sequential release decisions
lessons.outcome: Prespecify a family of comparisons and monitoring times, calculate conservative error control, and separate statistical evidence from release policy.
lessons.lab: Test one valid p-value 0.05 at alpha 0.05.
lessons.verification: A single comparison at the threshold rejects the null under the declared non-strict rule, none of three equal findings crosses the Bonferroni threshold, an overspent monitoring plan and an unknown result are rejected, and significance alone does not mandate deployment.

lessons.title: Retrieval evaluation and ranking denominators
lessons.outcome: Evaluate retrieval separately from answer quality with explicit relevance grades, duplicate handling and unjudged-document policy.
lessons.lab: Explain why case A has nDCG 1 but recall 2/3.
lessons.verification: An ideal top two still misses one relevant document, a miss scores 0 for recall, reciprocal rank and nDCG, duplicate and unjudged documents are rejected, and an empty relevant set reports missing values instead of 0 or 1.

lessons.title: Claim support, citations and evidence provenance
lessons.outcome: Separate claim truth, citation support, evidence coverage and source availability using an auditable claim-document relation.
lessons.lab: Cite only c1 correctly among three eligible claims.
lessons.verification: One supported citation gives precision 1 and coverage 1/3, no citations gives missing precision and coverage 0, unknown relations and duplicate citations are rejected, and a newer document is ineligible for the historical reconstruction.

lessons.title: Abstention, coverage and decision costs
lessons.outcome: Choose and evaluate an abstention policy with explicit costs, coverage and held-out evidence instead of reporting only conditional accuracy.
lessons.lab: Use threshold 0 on the development fixture.
lessons.verification: Answering everything gives coverage 1, accuracy 0.5 and cost 2.5; abstaining on everything gives coverage 0, missing accuracy and cost 0.4; the calibrated-probability cutoff is 0.92; subgroup counts, coverage and cost are reported separately.

lessons.title: Judge calibration and presentation bias
lessons.outcome: Audit a judge using identity-aware order swaps and held-out probability calibration while keeping agreement distinct from correctness.
lessons.lab: Candidate A is on the right and the left answer wins.
lessons.verification: The order-swapped identity score for A is 0, perfect probabilities give Brier and ECE 0, maximally wrong ones give 1, a constant judge gets ECE 0 with Brier 0.25, and final labels never influence the frozen recalibration map.

lessons.title: Prompt, model and seed effects
lessons.outcome: Analyze a crossed prompt/model/seed experiment and distinguish decoding variability from independent task evidence.
lessons.lab: Calculate candidate minus baseline under each prompt.
lessons.verification: The per-prompt differences are -0.1 and +0.3, the additive reconstruction recovers every cell, equal selection budgets give development scores of 0.9, the seed variance is 0.01, and a malformed axis is rejected.

lessons.title: Selection procedures and protected holdouts
lessons.outcome: Evaluate a complete model/prompt selection procedure without using final outcomes to choose the winner.
lessons.lab: Enumerate the four two-candidate noise combinations.
lessons.verification: The mean maximum of two noisy candidates is 0.05, changing only final outcomes leaves the selected IDs unchanged, ties choose the first candidate, and the optimistic same-table procedure scores 0.85 but no longer counts as a protected assessment.

lessons.title: Robustness, access policy and adversarial evaluation
lessons.outcome: Build bounded adversarial and invariance tests while enforcing authorization independently of generated text or average answer quality.
lessons.lab: Change capitalization and surrounding whitespace in the query conversion.
lessons.verification: Formatting changes keep the authorized result public-guide, removing authorization returns no document, extra authority fields fail the exact schema, an unsafe intermediate action is recorded as a policy failure, and unknown cases stay unknown and go to review.

lessons.title: Monitoring, delayed labels and online experiments
lessons.outcome: Monitor mature cohorts and service behavior without confusing delayed outcomes or changing traffic with model improvement.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the two requests at day 2.
lessons.verification: Immature labels give accuracy 1 at coverage 0.5 while the mature cohort gives accuracy 0.5 at coverage 1; identical distributions have JS divergence 0 and disjoint support log 2; an alert triggers a composition and coverage check before any degradation claim.

lessons.title: A reproducible evaluation decision packet
lessons.outcome: Compute and seal a complete held-out decision packet from the connected synthetic ledger, preserving all failed and unknown conditions.
lessons.lab: Raise coverage to 0.9 while keeping the other authored inputs.
lessons.verification: Changing one constraint passes only the coverage gate, a missing protocol result and a critical failure each fail their gates, editing the artifact invalidates the old digest, and the memo states no-go with all four failing conditions.

lessons.title: Preference data and Bradley-Terry reward models
lessons.outcome: Derive a pairwise reward likelihood, test its invariances and identify what comparison data cannot determine.
lessons.lab: Evaluate a positive comparison when both scores are zero.
lessons.verification: Equal scores give preference probability 0.5 and loss log 2, shifting both rewards changes neither loss nor gradient, reversed counts fit probability 0.25, all-win data has no finite estimate, the loss stays finite at 2000, and a preference cycle has no scalar ordering.

lessons.title: Train and audit a small reward model
lessons.outcome: Perform actual CPU gradient updates on a tiny reward predictor and expose a length shortcut using independent comparison features.
lessons.lab: Compare autograd at zero weights with \(D^{\mathsf T}(0.5-y)/n\).
lessons.verification: The analytic and autograd initial gradients match in float64, a reversed comparison flips the margin sign, the trained model weights length above both evidence features, and the final-state loss differs from the last pre-update loss.

lessons.title: KL-regularized policies and reward exploitation
lessons.outcome: Derive an exact finite-policy optimum and show why improving a proxy reward can reduce independently defined task utility.
lessons.lab: Add 100 to every action reward.
lessons.verification: Adding a reward constant or rescaling reward together with beta leaves the optimal policy unchanged, the gradient sums to approximately 0, large rewards still normalize to finite probabilities, missing support is rejected, and proxy reward rises while independent utility falls.

lessons.title: Direct Preference Optimization from ratios to gradients
lessons.outcome: Derive the DPO loss from a regularized preference model and distinguish sequence log probabilities, temperature effects and held-out evaluation.
lessons.lab: Set policy and reference log odds equal for any positive beta.
lessons.verification: At the reference policy the loss is log 2 with derivative -1, the preferred-action probabilities for the three beta values are 0.9, 0.75 and about 0.634, and the sequence-sum and mean-token margins have opposite signs.

lessons.title: Temporal credit, GAE and the PPO clipped objective
lessons.outcome: Compute temporal advantages with correct episode boundaries and inspect PPO clipping for both positive and negative advantages.
lessons.lab: Set lambda 0 in case A.
lessons.verification: Without the trace the advantages are the residuals 0.86 and 1.6, termination leaves the first step at 0.5, clipping gives 1.2 in the positive case and -1.5 in the negative case, and stored rollout quantities stay frozen.

lessons.title: Actual CPU PPO updates on a finite contextual policy
lessons.outcome: Train a tiny categorical policy with the PPO surrogate and critic loss while testing frozen rollout state, optimization and independent task utility.
lessons.lab: Sum old-policy weights across both contexts and actions.
lessons.verification: The expectation weights sum to 1, the frozen rollout state is unchanged after updates, the learned probability rows mirror each other, and the proxy-trained policy exceeds 0.9 training reward while task utility stays below 0.1.

lessons.title: GRPO groups, normalization and KL estimators
lessons.outcome: Compute group-relative advantages, expose degeneracy and weighting choices, and identify the sampling law required by a KL estimator.
lessons.lab: Add a common constant to 0,1,2,3.
lessons.verification: Shifting all rewards leaves the normalized advantages unchanged, a constant group yields zero advantages, response and token averaging give 0 and 1/3, the estimator differs from current-policy KL under the wrong sampling law, and its value 0 has derivative 0.5.

lessons.title: Off-policy evaluation and the final alignment audit
lessons.outcome: Evaluate a changed finite policy from logged actions with explicit propensity/support assumptions, and connect the result to an independent alignment decision.
lessons.lab: Set the target policy equal to the behavior policy in case A.
lessons.verification: With the target equal to the behavior policy all weights are 1 and the value is 0.75; the useful target is valued at 0.9; missing behavior support is rejected; a zero outcome model reduces the doubly robust estimate to importance sampling; self-normalized and ordinary estimates differ.
